title: Normalized exchange mates and finite pastes at specified inputs
statement: Use normalized compositors [def-pur-compact-scalar-site-compositors], word values and comparisons [def-pur-compact-scalar-site-words], and Cartesian open diagrams [def-pur-compact-scalar-site-diagram]. For a restriction exchange involving two open letters j,k and two direct letters p,q, an exchange identification consists of set-sheaf inverse-image exchanges in both systems satisfying the vertical set cube, and four ordinary module exchanges normalized by these same underlying-sheaf maps on every generalized section. Its restriction exchange is the geometric-adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the inverse of the exact descended identification. An inverse-exchange candidate is four natural transformations in the reverse direction. ValidAt requires them to be mutually inverse to the specified restriction exchanges only at I_j(M_A),I_j(M_B) and the corresponding tilde-open images of N_X(M_A),N_X(M_B). The open exchange comparison I_k R_q→R_p I_j is defined by the inverse mate bijection for the two open adjunctions, applied to this inverse candidate. Define vertical and horizontal pastes of comparisons by composition and whiskering, and identity comparisons by identity transformations. A reverse comparison is inverse at specified inputs if its four components are mutually inverse there. PasteAt is the inductively generated proposition for identity comparisons, the specified direct and open compositors, open exchange comparisons with ValidAt, vertical pastes, horizontal pastes (with the second input evaluated by the target first factor), and these inputwise inverses. It is syntax for normalized finite pastes and imposes no site-square or scalar-square equation as a constructor hypothesis.
